items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: it was Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, it was Art Blakey, Dexter Gordon and Gene Ammons, and Tommy Potter, myself, Don Byas, and a couple of other people I can't remember.

ctx.x: Around that time, 1945, after playing the Apollo Theatre, we started our trek South again. We played the Apollo Theatre that Christmas, I believe, or during Christmas week or the holiday week, and after that we started to trek South in early 1945.

I do remember on New Year's Eve, just before 1945, they had a session, I guess, a Jazz concert, at a place called Manhattan Square. I've forgotten who it was that produced this thing, but it was Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, it was Art Blakey, Dexter Gordon and Gene Ammons, and Tommy Potter, myself, Don Byas, and a couple of other people I can't remember. But I still have this waiver that they had that advertised is. I still have it at home.

The funny part about it was, they had all sorts of accolades that they paid tribute to different artists. I remember at the top of it, they advertised this thing as "Dizzy Gillespie, The Wizard of the Trumpet. Dexter Gordon, A Weird Tenor Man. Gene Ammons Blows Like Mad. Sarah Vaughan
